critiques.description: Control mapping map-015 classifies req-LOG-001 as not applicable by asserting that leakage through logs is not part of thr-001, even though the threat definition for thr-001 explicitly lists logs as a possible way an attacker could obtain a download link.
critiques.rationale: The applicability_reason for map-015 states that although logs may exist, "leakage of sensitive data through logs is not part of this threat, and controlling log content would not prevent or materially change the unauthorized download described." However, thr-001’s preconditions explicitly describe an attacker obtaining or guessing a download link "for example, via logs, misdirected communication, browser history, or weakly unguessable identifiers," which makes log content and destinations part of the modeled attack surface for this threat. Operations documentation also confirms that export activity is logged and monitored (evd-007), so logging is a real subsystem, not a hypothetical. Given that, it is internally inconsistent to both (a) treat log-based exposure as a precondition for thr-001 and (b) declare that a requirement about controlling log content (req-LOG-001) "does not bear" on the scenario. The mapping should be revised either to treat req-LOG-001 as applicable to thr-001’s log-based leak paths or to update the threat definition if logs are truly intended to be out of scope.

critiques.description: Documentation gap gap-015 duplicates the contradiction already captured in gap-003 about export file retention behaviour and its inconsistent documentation, with substantially overlapping importance and requested evidence.
critiques.rationale: Both gap-003 and gap-015 are based on the same two passages: the architecture overview describing export files as temporary working data deleted immediately once downloaded (evd-003) and the operations guide describing a 30-day storage lifecycle policy for completed export files (evd-006). Each gap cites this contradiction, notes that the actual retention behaviour and its alignment with customer-facing expectations cannot be determined, and requests essentially the same clarifications about the canonical retention behaviour, customer-facing documentation, and which document is authoritative. The only material difference is which threat identifiers they list as related objects, but the underlying documentation issue is the same. Maintaining two separate gaps for the same inconsistency adds noise without improving coverage, so these should be merged into a single retention-behaviour documentation gap that references all relevant threats and requirements.
